findings.highlight: I desperately try to avoid the strike, but I can't.
findings.evidenceJa: 身をひねって躱すも、薄皮一枚とはいかない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou twists away, but not by a mere paper-thin margin: the nonfatal cut still slices flesh and may become fatal.
findings.explanation: A partially successful evasion becomes a failed attempt to evade.

findings.highlight: I am the bone of my sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 体は、剣で出来ている。
findings.governingReading: The memories interleave altered Japanese lines: body made of swords; blood iron and heart glass; undefeated battle, no retreat, no understanding; solitary intoxication with victory on the hill of swords; and a life without meaning.
findings.explanation: Five scene-specific Japanese chant variants are replaced by unrelated stock English Unlimited Blade Works lines.

findings.highlight: Look. This where you'll end up.
findings.evidenceJa: 見ろ　これが貴様の結末だ。
findings.governingReading: Archer demands that Shirou look at his own future endpoint.
findings.explanation: A climactic warning drops its copula.

findings.highlight: He holds his breath.
findings.evidenceJa: 息が止まる。
findings.governingReading: The first-person sequence remains in Shirou's viewpoint: his breath stops because Archer is about to verbalize the memories he saw.
findings.explanation: Shirou holding his breath becomes Archer holding his breath.

findings.highlight: I've just been playing tough, pretending that my broken heart is whole.
findings.evidenceJa: 折れかかった心が、まだ折れていないと強がっている。
findings.governingReading: Shirou's nearly broken heart bluffs that it is not broken yet, allowing the body to demand continued resistance.
findings.explanation: A heart close to breaking but insisting it has not broken becomes a broken heart pretending to be whole.

findings.highlight: Trace, on. (Begin Projection.)
findings.evidenceJa: 投影、完了
findings.governingReading: After assembling all eight stages, Shirou says 'Projection, complete'; the ruby marks Trace Off.
findings.explanation: Projection completion and Trace Off become Projection commencement and Trace On.

findings.highlight: Your dream, huh?
findings.evidenceJa: じいさんの夢は、俺が
findings.governingReading: The remembered fragment begins 'Old man, your dream—I will...', the casual sentence that relieved Kiritsugu and converted admiration into obligation.
findings.explanation: Shirou's promise to inherit his old man's dream becomes a vague question about that dream.

findings.highlight: A man even emptier than me heard my innocent words, entrusted his wish to me in relief, and passed away.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の何気ない言葉を聞いて、安心したと遺して、俺以上に空っぽだった人は逝った。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu heard Shirou's offhand statement, left the word 'relieved,' and died; the burden is the consequence Shirou formed from that response.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu dying relieved by Shirou's casual words becomes explicitly entrusting Shirou with his wish.

findings.highlight: what Kiritsugu failed to become
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮切嗣という男がなりたかったモノ
findings.governingReading: Archer calls Shirou's ideal an imitation of the thing Kiritsugu wanted to be and believed right.
findings.explanation: What Kiritsugu wanted to become becomes what he failed to become.

findings.highlight: I scrounge up every bit of mental focus I have left to create a Kanshou, and just barely deflect another slash.
findings.evidenceJa: 残った全精力で作り上げた干将も、わずか一撃で歪曲した。
findings.governingReading: The Kanshou made with all his remaining strength is already present; a single blow warps it.
findings.explanation: A projected Kanshou distorting from one hit becomes Shirou creating it and barely deflecting the hit.

findings.highlight: Kanshou breaks, and my life begins to peter out.
findings.evidenceJa: その干将も歪に折れ曲がり、存在そのものが薄れかかっている。
findings.governingReading: The distorted Kanshou bends and its own existence grows thin; Shirou then feels pain in his chest from Archer's words.
findings.explanation: Kanshou bending and fading becomes Kanshou breaking while Shirou's life fades.

findings.highlight: Your hypocrisy can't save anyything.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな偽善では何も救えない。
findings.governingReading: Archer says such hypocrisy cannot save anything.
findings.explanation: A typographical error mars Archer's accusation.

findings.highlight: I sail through the air, not unlike during the encounter with Berserker.
findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーもかくやという一撃は、たやすく衛宮士郎の体を弾き飛ばす。
findings.governingReading: The force that sends Shirou flying is one even Berserker might have delivered.
findings.explanation: A Berserker-like blow becomes a comparison to Shirou's earlier encounter with Berserker.

findings.highlight: Your ideals are morally bankrupt.
findings.evidenceJa: その理想は破綻している。
findings.governingReading: Archer calls the ideal broken or untenable, then describes its aspirations as a fairy tale.
findings.explanation: English makes Archer's condemnation explicitly moral, where the Japanese calls the ideal untenable and explains it as a fairy tale.

findings.highlight: If my weapons are broken, I'll just use them as they are.
findings.evidenceJa: 壊れているなら壊れていないところを使えばいい。
findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that if he is broken, he must use whatever part remains unbroken, then reach into still-untouched inner territory.
findings.explanation: Using unbroken parts of a broken body becomes using broken weapons as they are.

findings.highlight: My body is made of swords. (I am the bone of my sword.)
findings.evidenceJa: I am the bone of my sword.
findings.governingReading: The source foregrounds the English 'I am the bone of my sword' as the uttered spell.
findings.explanation: The English incantation and Japanese gloss trade places at Shirou's recovery beat.

findings.highlight: I followed in Kiritsugu's footsteps because it's a dream that won't come true and an impossible ideal.
findings.evidenceJa: 叶わない夢、有り得ない理想だからこそ、切嗣は追い続けた。
findings.governingReading: Shirou recognizes that Kiritsugu continued pursuing the dream precisely despite knowing it could not be realized.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu pursuing an impossible ideal becomes Shirou following him because it was impossible.

findings.highlight: He wields his longsword with swift skill.
findings.evidenceJa: 咄嗟に長剣を返し、振るわれる一刀を捌く。
findings.governingReading: He instantly reverses his longsword and handles/parries Shirou's swinging blade.
findings.explanation: Archer parrying one incoming stroke becomes merely wielding his sword skillfully.

findings.highlight: He cries out, his muscles begging for oxygen. They demand that he stop due to a lack of blood.
findings.evidenceJa: 筋肉は酸素を求めて悲鳴をあげ、足りなすぎる血液は運動停止を命じ続ける。
findings.governingReading: His muscles scream for oxygen and his critically low blood volume continually commands activity to stop.
findings.explanation: Shirou cries out instead of his oxygen-starved muscles.

findings.highlight: The boy's accepted that each swing of his sword will be hellish suffering.
findings.evidenceJa: 振るう一撃は地獄の苦しみと同意の筈だ。
findings.governingReading: From Archer's viewpoint, every blow must be equivalent to the torment of hell for the dying boy.
findings.explanation: Each sword swing necessarily equaling hellish suffering becomes suffering Shirou has accepted.

findings.highlight: It seems to offend his stubbornly persistent enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 死に損ないの敵も癇に障るが
findings.governingReading: Archer receives the blows irritably; the half-dead enemy grates on his nerves, as does his own refusal to step back.
findings.explanation: Archer being irritated by the persistent dying enemy becomes the enemy being offended.

findings.highlight: The memories come unbidden, and I swore that I'd never let this happen again.
findings.evidenceJa: いわれもなく無意味に消えていく思い出を見て、二度と、こんな事は繰り返させないと誓った。
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls the people he could not save and the self that was not saved, seeing those memories disappear causelessly and meaninglessly, and vows against repetition.
findings.explanation: Memories of people vanishing without reason become memories arriving unbidden.

findings.highlight: I'll make the dream come true.
findings.evidenceJa: 叶わないと。
findings.governingReading: The fragment 'It won't come true' introduces Kiritsugu, who saved Shirou as a child and died leaving the dream behind sadly.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu saying the dream cannot come true becomes Shirou promising to make it come true.

findings.highlight: Even if the whole world shuns me and the oath turns out to be a curse, I won't give it up.
findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の人間に疎まれても、こうして自分自身に呪われても、それだけは—
findings.governingReading: Even if the world hates him and he curses his own self in this confrontation, he will not relinquish the wish.
findings.explanation: Shirou being cursed by himself becomes the oath turning out to be a curse.

findings.highlight: The enemy flicks his sword and re-sheathes it in a single, large stance.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣を弾き、一際大きく剣を構え直す敵の姿。
findings.governingReading: After deflecting Archer's blade, Shirou readies his sword again in an especially large posture for the final strike.
findings.explanation: Shirou resetting into a large sword stance becomes re-sheathing the sword.

findings.highlight: The impact breaks one of my limbs.
findings.evidenceJa: どちらかの腕と足が折れた。
findings.governingReading: The impact breaks one of Shirou's arms and one of his legs; their sides are not yet identified.
findings.explanation: One arm and one leg breaking becomes one unspecified limb breaking.

findings.highlight: The enemy's left arm is wide open.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵の左胸はがら空きだ。
findings.governingReading: Archer's left chest is open; he swings the longsword back to guard it, and for him that defense should easily arrive in time.
findings.explanation: Archer's exposed left chest and easy defensive return become an exposed left arm and closing distance.

findings.highlight: the gears never turn in his head
findings.evidenceJa: その歯車はかみ合わないまま
findings.governingReading: Shirou's determined blow and Archer's defense, which should arrive in time, fail to interlock; even Archer does not know why he failed to parry.
findings.explanation: Attack and defense failing to mesh becomes mental gears failing to turn.
